label: Bible Study
prompt: Husbands, love your _____, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it;
verse: Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it;
note: Paul's standard for husbands — love measured by Christ's self-giving.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Thou hast enlarged my steps under me; so that my feet did not _____.
verse: Thou hast enlarged my steps under me; so that my feet did not slip.
note: God widened the path under David's steps so his feet would not slip.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And he had a son, whose name was Saul, a choice young man, and a goodly: and there was not among the children of Israel a goodlier person than he: from his _____ and upward he was higher than any of the people.
verse: And he had a son, whose name was Saul, a choice young man, and a goodly: and there was not among the children of Israel a goodlier person than he: from his shoulders and upward he was higher than any of the people.
note: Saul looked the part: from his shoulders upward he was taller than anyone in Israel.

label: Deep Water
prompt: If thou hast run with the _____, and they have wearied thee, then how canst thou contend with horses? and if in the land of peace, wherein thou trustedst, they wearied thee, then how wilt thou do in the swelling of Jordan?
verse: If thou hast run with the footmen, and they have wearied thee, then how canst thou contend with horses? and if in the land of peace, wherein thou trustedst, they wearied thee, then how wilt thou do in the swelling of Jordan?
note: Jeremiah complained about his troubles; God answered that things were going to get harder.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: But I have all, and abound: I am full, having received of Epaphroditus the things which were sent from you, an _____ of a sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable, wellpleasing to God.
verse: But I have all, and abound: I am full, having received of Epaphroditus the things which were sent from you, an odour of a sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable, wellpleasing to God.
note: The Philippians' gift, carried by Epaphroditus, was 'an odour of a sweet smell' — the KJV spells it British.
